title: The Transistor: Physical Root of Digital Hardware (1947)
explainer: On December 16, 1947, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain at Bell Labs demonstrated the first working point-contact transistor, the solid-state replacement for the vacuum tube that eventually made every register, GPIO pin, and logic gate in a microcontroller possible. Bare-metal programming — directly manipulating memory-mapped hardware registers — is about as close as software gets to the physical switching behavior that Bardeen, Brattain, and William Shockley discovered, for which the three shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.
